companies.name: Google DeepMind
companies.description: World-leading AI research lab; developed GameNGen, Genie 3/D4RT world models, Veo and SynthID.
companies.officeFunction: London headquarters and core research centre for frontier models, world models and interactive-environment research.

companies.name: Stability AI
companies.description: Creator of Stable Diffusion and open image, audio and video foundation models used in game-production pipelines.
companies.officeFunction: London AI model research and product location focused on generative media models, APIs and enterprise deployment rather than direct game production.

companies.name: Synthesia
companies.description: Enterprise text-to-video avatar platform relevant to synthetic presenters and localised game cinematics.
companies.officeFunction: London product and engineering location for avatar generation, multilingual video, lip-sync and enterprise digital-agent workflows.

companies.name: ElevenLabs
companies.description: Generative voice and speech platform used to vocalise dynamic NPC and narrator dialogue.
companies.officeFunction: London product and engineering hub for multilingual speech models, voice agents and developer APIs relevant to runtime game characters.

companies.name: VEED.io
companies.description: AI-assisted video editing and content platform relevant to game marketing and creator workflows.
companies.officeFunction: London product hub for browser-based editing, automated subtitles, translation, clipping and video enhancement used by game community and marketing teams.

companies.name: Colossyan
companies.description: Synthetic-video platform relevant to scalable training, localisation and internal content production.
companies.officeFunction: London product and engineering location for AI presenters, script-to-video generation, localisation and enterprise learning content.

companies.name: UK AI Safety Institute
companies.description: UK government body conducting frontier-model evaluations and AI safety research.
companies.officeFunction: London public-sector research and evaluation location for model testing, safety methods and evidence that informs UK AI policy; it does not develop commercial games.

companies.name: UK ICO
companies.description: UK data-protection regulator overseeing privacy, automated decisions and AI transparency.
companies.officeFunction: Primary regulatory office for UK GDPR enforcement and guidance affecting player profiling, voice data, biometrics, conversational memory and AI analytics.

companies.name: Ubisoft Montreal / La Forge
companies.description: Lead studio behind Watch Dogs 2 and a core Ubisoft La Forge research location.
companies.officeFunction: AAA production plus applied R&D linking academic work in AI and machine learning to game prototypes and production tools. Watch Dogs 2's systemic civilian AI and multi-agent coordination originated in this production ecosystem.
relevantProducts: La Forge AI and machine-learning prototypes

companies.name: Mistral AI
companies.description: European open-weight language-model developer supplying sovereign and enterprise AI models.
companies.officeFunction: Paris model-research and product hub for open-weight LLMs and enterprise inference that can underpin game tools, agents and European deployments.

companies.name: Black Forest Labs
companies.description: Developer of FLUX open-weight image models used for concept art, textures and visual ideation.
companies.officeFunction: Freiburg research and model-development location for text-to-image generation, visual model tooling and provenance methods relevant to game-asset workflows.

companies.name: Smartly.io
companies.description: Automated advertising technology relevant to scaled, localised game campaigns and user acquisition.
companies.officeFunction: Helsinki product and engineering location for campaign automation, creative optimisation and AI-assisted localisation rather than in-game AI development.

companies.name: European Commission
companies.description: EU institution responsible for AI Act implementation and major digital-market enforcement.
companies.officeFunction: Brussels policy and enforcement location overseeing the EU AI Office, AI Act implementation, DMA and DSA; relevant to generative game content, GPAI providers and platform conduct.

companies.name: EDPB
companies.description: European Data Protection Board coordinating GDPR interpretation and cross-border enforcement.
companies.officeFunction: Brussels regulatory coordination location for European privacy rules affecting player telemetry, conversational memory, voice data, profiling and cross-border AI processing.

companies.name: Rockstar North
companies.description: Lead Grand Theft Auto studio and major contributor to Rockstar's large-scale open-world systems.
companies.officeFunction: Core Grand Theft Auto production: open-world architecture, mission and world design, NPC population systems and integration of shared Rockstar technology. Public claims that GTA VI uses machine-learning NPCs remain unconfirmed.
relevantProducts: Shared Rockstar navigation and animation technology

companies.name: Creative Assembly
companies.description: Sega-owned development studio behind Alien: Isolation's layered director and Xenomorph AI.
companies.officeFunction: Game development and technology centre responsible for Alien: Isolation's macro tension director, local enemy behavior trees, perception, search and pathfinding.

companies.name: Hello Games
companies.description: Independent development studio behind No Man's Sky's continuous procedural universe.
companies.officeFunction: Core design and engineering studio for seeded planet generation, terrain, textures, vegetation, fauna, population systems and ongoing live updates.
relevantProducts: No Man's Sky continuous world generation

companies.name: Lo-Fi Games
companies.description: Independent studio behind Kenshi's autonomous faction and squad simulation.
companies.officeFunction: Core development location for Kenshi's goal and job packages, faction relations, autonomous settlements and persistent world-state simulation.

companies.name: Embark Studios
companies.description: Development studio behind ARC Raiders and its bounded machine-learning locomotion systems.
companies.officeFunction: Primary game-development and technology studio. Selected ARC machines use reinforcement-learned locomotion controllers; combat strategy remains in authored systems. The team also integrates authorised text-to-speech vocabulary.

sources.label: Embark explains ARC Raiders AI use

companies.name: Warhorse Studios
companies.description: Development studio behind Kingdom Come: Deliverance's schedule-driven medieval world simulation.
companies.officeFunction: Core game-development location for NPC daily cycles, fallback behavior, world-state reactions and historically grounded open-world simulation.

companies.name: GSC Game World
companies.description: Development studio behind the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series and its A-Life simulation architecture.
companies.officeFunction: Game-development location for the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. franchise. A-Life simulates actors, goals and encounters beyond the player's immediate area before switching them into detailed local behavior.

companies.name: Rockstar San Diego / RAGE Technology Group
companies.description: Rockstar development and central technology location associated with Red Dead and the RAGE engine.
companies.officeFunction: Distinct from Rockstar North's GTA production role: this location leads Red Dead development and shared RAGE engine technology spanning graphics, physics, animation, networking, AI and character behavior.
relevantProducts: Red Dead Redemption 2 horse and wildlife AI
RAGE engine AI and character systems
Shared Rockstar physics and animation tools

companies.name: Ubisoft Toronto / La Forge
companies.description: Lead production studio for Watch Dogs: Legion and a Ubisoft La Forge research location.
companies.officeFunction: Unlike Montreal's Watch Dogs 2 and broader R&D role, Toronto led Watch Dogs: Legion and its Play as Anyone/Census systems for procedural citizens, schedules, relationships and mission casting.

companies.name: Ubisoft Winnipeg
companies.description: Technology-focused Ubisoft studio supporting shared engines and large-scale game systems.
companies.officeFunction: Engine and platform technology rather than lead narrative production: works on Anvil, Snowdrop and Scalar, contributes to Watch Dogs: Legion, and develops shared technology for larger simulations and future games.

companies.name: Monolith Productions / WB Games
companies.description: Studio responsible for F.E.A.R.'s GOAP combat AI and the patented Nemesis System.
companies.officeFunction: Core game-development studio for tactical planning and persistent procedural characters. Its systems span F.E.A.R.'s real-time action planning and Shadow of Mordor/War's memory, hierarchy, rivalry and dialogue framework.
relevantProducts: Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War

companies.name: Bethesda Game Studios
companies.description: Core Bethesda studio associated with The Elder Scrolls and Fallout's Radiant systems.
companies.officeFunction: Lead franchise design and engineering location for schedule-driven NPC packages, Radiant AI, Radiant Story quest templates and persistent open-world simulation.
relevantProducts: Skyrim Radiant AI and Radiant Story

companies.name: Naughty Dog / Sony Interactive Entertainment
companies.description: Lead studio for The Last of Us franchise and its enemy, companion and melee AI systems.
companies.officeFunction: Game-development centre for partial-knowledge enemy searches, paired investigation, companion cover selection and modular melee behavior. Sony's wider AI research is separate from this production studio.
relevantProducts: The Last of Us Part I search and companion AI
The Last of Us Part II vague-knowledge perception

sources.label: The Last of Us Part I gameplay systems
The Last of Us Part II melee AI — GDC

companies.name: Valve
companies.description: Valve's development base for games, Source technology and the Steam platform.
companies.officeFunction: Game and platform engineering location associated with Left 4 Dead's AI Director, NextBot navigation and encounter pacing, alongside Source and Steam technology.

sources.label: Valve — AI Systems of Left 4 Dead

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.description: Core NVIDIA engineering headquarters for GPU, inference and game-AI platforms including ACE.
companies.officeFunction: Platform R&D rather than game production: develops ACE language, speech, animation and inference components integrated by studios such as Krafton and Meaning Machine.

companies.name: Tripo AI / VAST
companies.description: 3D foundation model and world-model company; creator of Project Eden, Tripo GameHub, and the Tripo developer API for text/image-to-3D generation, rigging and animation.
companies.officeFunction: San Francisco research and product headquarters. VAST AI Research develops Project Eden — a persistent multiplayer world model with multi-agent interaction. The Tripo API powers game-asset pipelines (Unity, Unreal, Cocos, Godot plugins), and GameHub is an AI-3D powered game creation platform.

companies.name: Electronic Arts Montreal
companies.description: EA technology hub combining studio development with shared engine, analytics and research teams.
companies.officeFunction: Distinct from EA's publishing headquarters: hosts Motive, Frostbite contributors, analytics, user research, SEED and audio technology teams supporting simulation, believable characters and shared production tools.

sources.label: Official EA locations and team functions
